python3 << 'EOF'
import math

# 1979 data (from treasury_bulletin_1980_03_page_88.txt)
treasury_1979 = [8.43, 8.43, 8.45, 8.44, 8.55, 8.32, 8.35, 8.42, 8.68, 9.44, 9.80, 9.58]
corporate_1979 = [9.47, 9.52, 9.65, 9.69, 9.82, 9.51, 9.47, 9.57, 9.87, 11.17, 11.52, 11.30]

# 1984 data (from treasury_bulletin_1985_03_page_48.txt)
treasury_1984 = [11.82, 12.00, 12.45, 12.65, 13.43, 13.54, 13.36, 12.71, 12.42, 12.04, 11.66, 11.64]
corporate_1984 = [12.65, 12.80, 13.36, 13.64, 14.41, 14.49, 14.25, 13.54, 13.37, 13.02, 12.40, 12.47]

def pearson_correlation(x, y):
    n = len(x)
    mean_x = sum(x) / n
    mean_y = sum(y) / n
    
    numerator = sum((x[i] - mean_x) * (y[i] - mean_y) for i in range(n))
    
    sum_sq_x = sum((xi - mean_x) ** 2 for xi in x)
    sum_sq_y = sum((yi - mean_y) ** 2 for yi in y)
    
    denominator = math.sqrt(sum_sq_x * sum_sq_y)
    
    return numerator / denominator

# Calculate correlations
corr_1979 = pearson_correlation(treasury_1979, corporate_1979)
corr_1984 = pearson_correlation(treasury_1984, corporate_1984)

print(f"1979 Pearson correlation: {corr_1979}")
print(f"1984 Pearson correlation: {corr_1984}")

# Absolute difference
abs_diff = abs(corr_1979 - corr_1984)
print(f"Absolute difference: {abs_diff}")
print(f"Absolute difference rounded to 4 decimal places: {abs_diff:.4f}")
EOF

    # For sample correlation, we divide by n-1

    sum_sq_y = sum((yi - mean_y) ** 2 for yi in y)
    
    # The formula r = Σ(xi - x̄)(yi - ȳ) / √[Σ(xi - x̄)²Σ(yi - ȳ)²]
    # is actually the population correlation. For sample, we could use n or n-1,
    # but it cancels out so the result is the same.
    denominator = math.sqrt(sum_sq_x * sum_sq_y)
    
    return numerator / denominator
